messages:
marco: I opened a compact handbook patch that consolidates reserved-pool onboarding examples + a tiny troubleshooting note about isolation labeling. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/2619. Can docs + infra eyeball?

devdocs: jumping in. We should prefer 'account' vs 'tenant' everywhere. Also add a minimal terraform snippet and a short autoscale example so folks can copy-paste.

leo: added TF snippet and an HCL comment about preemption semantics. Snippet in PR: ```hcl
resource "redwood_reserved_pool" "acme_prod" {
  account = "acme-prod"
  gpus = 2
  region = "us-west-2"
  labels = { env = "prod", team = "ml" }
}
```

infra-bot: CI: docs-lint OK. linkcheck: flagged one stale path -> /terraform-examples/dedicated/reserved_pool.tf (suggested replacement /infra-samples/terraform/dedicated/reserved_pool.tf).

marco: thanks. For the autoscale example I drafted two short profiles in the PR: one for latency-sensitive apps and one for throughput. Please sanity-check cooldowns.

devdocs: suggested values look reasonable. My edit: use 30s scaleUp & 300s scaleDown for latency-sensitive, and 60s/180s with higher burst for throughput. Add a line: "Burst instances are preemptible under host pressure."

leo: pushed the YAML examples and switched wording to 'account' in onboarding steps. Also added a tiny SDK snippet (py) using current client API: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'))
res = client.dedicated.create_reservation(account_id='acme-prod', gpus=2, region='us-west-2')
print(res)
```

marco: perfect. Remaining blockers: legal to sign off on the handbook SLA phrase (short line in the doc) and infra to confirm the playbook redirect exists. I'll ping legal and infra and merge after approvals.
